_doc: Generic example routing menu. Copy to private configuration and set AGENTGLIM_JEV_ROUTES to customize. No usage state or timed pauses are packaged.
stateTemplate:
A coordinator is about to hand this job to a subagent. Job:
{task}
modelQuestion: Is {desc} the single best choice of agent for this job, weighing quality needed against cost and scarce usage limits?
effortQuestion: The job will run on {name}. Is {effortDesc} the right reasoning effort: enough for the job without wasting time and usage?

effortDesc.max: maximum reasoning (hardest, highest stakes, cost no object)

design._doc: Rule: design jobs always go to a Claude model, never to a local model. Before stage 1, Jev answers one noul question; at or above threshold the job counts as design and only the 'allowed' options are asked and ranked (the strength order and tie margin still apply, so Opus beats Fable on a close call). If the design call fails, the job counts as design when any keyword appears as a word in it.
design.question: Is this job mainly visual or UI design: pages, layout, styling, icons, charts, themes, design-system work?

simple._doc: Rule: the local Qwen option is only for absolutely simple, self-contained plain-text or coding jobs (a single file, a clear spec; no multi-file debugging, no design, no investigation). Reason: a multi-file debug job routed to local Qwen ran 1 h, timed out and changed nothing. Asked in the same Jev call as the design question, before stage 1: below threshold, or for a design job, the 'gated' options are dropped from the menu. If that Jev call fails, the job counts as simple only when no keyword appears as a word, it is at most maxChars long and it names at most maxFiles files (ignoreFiles not counted). plans/_run/bin/worker.sh asks the same gate (jev-route.mjs --local-ok -f <task file>) before it gives a build task to a local Qwen lane.
simple.question: Is this an absolutely simple, self-contained plain-text or coding task: one file, a clear spec, no multi-file debugging, no design work and no investigation or research?

usage._doc: Rule: routing also weighs usage, with the tiers set on the AgentGlim page (modes.json 5h role gates usageLimit/overnightLimit, weekly caps, the budget ladder), read from the budget the driver writes every tick (file). No thresholds here: tier 1 full speed, tier 2 slowed (budget step 6-8, the Status page's 'slowed' pill), tier 3 paused or stopped (the role's 5h gate is shut, or step 9, limited or off). A tier-3 option leaves the menu; a tier-2 option loses close calls and Jev is told the tiers. A design job keeps its Claude options even at tier 3 and the plain line says OVER. map: option -> [budget provider ('go|go2' = the better of the two), role slot]; options not listed (free, local) are not limited. A missing or stale budget (older than _run/config.json budgetStaleS) changes nothing and shows 'usage: unknown'.

notify.title: Jev picked {pick}
notify.body: {pick} at {effort} effort for: {task90}. Heavy token use: this is the most expensive tier.

claude-fable.desc: Claude Fable: Anthropic's top model, for the very hardest, highest-stakes reasoning, design and review where cost does not matter

claude-opus.desc: Claude Opus: strong at hard reasoning, architecture, security or git-history work, careful multi-file refactors and final reviews

claude-sonnet.desc: Claude Sonnet: solid mid-size coding, UI changes, research and summaries that need good judgment but are not critical

claude-haiku.desc: Claude Haiku: quick simple lookups, file scans, checklists and short status reports with no tricky judgment

codex-astra.desc: OpenAI Codex Astra: OpenAI's top coding model, for the hardest long autonomous coding and debugging jobs

codex-sol.desc: OpenAI Codex Sol: strong long autonomous coding inside one repo, tests, builds and audits

codex-terra.desc: OpenAI Codex Terra: mid-tier Codex for routine implementation and fixes

codex-luna.desc: OpenAI Codex Luna: light, cheap Codex for small coding tasks and orchestration

opencode-free.desc: free OpenCode models: low-stakes bulk work, drafts, simple scripts; often rate limited

deepseek-flash.desc: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash via Pi: cheap fast coding and text edits of medium difficulty

local-qwen.desc: local Qwen3.6 on this machine: free and private, slower and weaker; simple private tasks, no web
